# Soul Economy

## Diegetic Meaning

Within Hera, souls are not merely inhabitants or the dead. To Ether Entities, they possess economic and energetic value. Souls can serve as food, a source of power, a medium of exchange, collateral, or part of a pact.

## Differences in Quality

A soul's value increases through:

- strength and developed abilities;
- extraordinary experiences;
- powerful bonds and memories;
- trials overcome;
- heroic or consequential deeds;
- a strongly developed will of its own.

This system explains why Jator and Semm do not harvest an arbitrary soul, but deliberately construct a heroic journey.

## Influence on Era

Because entities cannot enter Era directly, an indirect market arises around:

- traders and intermediaries;
- promises and pacts;
- corrupted individuals or institutions;
- hidden cults;
- objects that bind or redirect souls;
- offers of power in exchange for a later claim on the soul.

## Separation of Lore and Player Resource

The soul economy must not automatically mean that the player treats souls like ordinary coins. In the base game, only the Talisman is capable of gathering Soul Energy in a controlled way. The moral and metaphysical significance of this act must remain visible in the narrative.
